rationale: ⚠️ Empty random is accepted despite matching integer types in specification and handler; permissive binding bypasses the numeric contract.
The supplied order ID exceeds int64. Long conversion correctly rejects it; the checker treats unbounded Python integers as valid int64 values.
A form-created pet stores string tags and later returns them. The typed Tag model and independently constructed seed tags establish the object contract.
Positive ID 13 yields 500; the controller throws on positive IDs. A lookup rejection must not become an internal server error.
⚠️ Empty random receives 200 although both the specification and numeric handler require an integer token; no independent empty-value policy is documented.
Unchecked Optional.get crashes for missing product 0. The specification and dedicated missing-entity handler support 404; documenting this accidental 500 is unnecessary.
The required path parameter has no placeholder and is unused. An integration test explicitly posts favourites without a path ID and expects 204.
⚠️ Percent-encoded control characters receive 200 on a numeric-ID endpoint. The long handler agrees with the integer specification; acceptance defeats that boundary.
Product 0 is absent; unchecked Optional.get raises NoSuchElementException instead of the documented 404. This is the same observed crash as E006.
An omitted optional name filter is dereferenced unconditionally in TagDao.find. It can be handled as an absent filter; no required resource key is missing.
Status __main__ is accepted and persisted despite the matching enum in specification and model annotation. The implementation never enforces the declared allowable values.
⚠️ Object-like strings are accepted for featured. The Boolean handler and boolean query predicate support the specified boolean contract, rather than arbitrary text.
Listing tags without an optional name filter reaches name.toUpperCase on null. The stack trace identifies an implementation crash, not an environmental failure.
Representative ID overflows int64; other cluster rejections include an illegal control character in api_key. These are checker/generator false positives, with no valid-input rejection demonstrated.
Empty registration data reaches a null keyType switch without validation. Tests require 400 for missing keys; the specification also omits required key and keyType.
A syntactically valid but unknown TAN empties the Optional; unchecked get produces 500. The specification and controller documentation explicitly require 404 when verification fails.
The shared guard rejects omitted group although the specification makes it optional. Integration tests independently require unfiltered tag listing to succeed.
⚠️ Encoded control characters receive 200 as a category ID despite the long handler and integer specification. There is no documented textual-ID interpretation.
The roles handler returns 418, but an independent integration test explicitly expects 200, matching the specification. The implementation violates the intended success status.
The order ID exceeds signed int64. Rejecting Long conversion is correct; the checker fails to enforce the declared numeric format and reports valid rejection.
Product listing returns 418, while independent REST documentation explicitly specifies 200. The lone 418 statement contradicts documented intent, so this is implementation attribution.
The response echoes invalid status __main__. Both the model annotation and response schema specify the same enum; missing validation propagates an out-of-contract value.
Name is absent and explicitly WRITE_ONLY in code, but no independent evidence establishes that policy. Specification correction versus serialization/validation repair remains unresolved under v0.5.
Even a named seed pet omits name, matching WRITE_ONLY serialization. Repetition confirms behavior but supplies no independent intent evidence; v0.5 leaves attribution unresolved.
The group-null guard rejects an unfiltered request. Integration tests explicitly perform that request and expect 200, independently supporting the specification's optional group.
The form supplies name but the response omits it; WRITE_ONLY explains suppression. Independent support for that policy is absent, leaving this name-specific violation undecidable.
⚠️ Encoded control characters receive 200 on a media-file lookup. The long parameter corroborates numeric-ID intent; no independent policy authorizes this noninteger input.
Optional tags are rejected when absent or empty. Only one explicit guard supports requiring tags; no independent policy evidence resolves specification versus implementation attribution.
A nameless XML pet is stored and later returned without required name. Ordinary name serialization and named seed pets support a validation defect, not intentional suppression.
